rationale:
The bugs_open/305 council round (c48b7612, APPROVED) left one advisory from the reuse_agent seat: the truncation three-state (known-at-ceiling / known-below / UNKNOWN) is inline in rewrite_negations_action.go and wants to be a shared helper — and whoever takes it should AUDIT the other call sites rather than move one. This is that follow-up, and the audit changed its shape.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND (as of 2026-08-22). Non-test code comparing output tokens to a ceiling: THREE sites — rewrite_negations_action.go:535 (mine), and cmd/reasoningset/main.go:684 and :706. Three further grep hits (provocation_gate_action.go:532, provocation_generator_action.go:224, diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:1248) are COMMENTS citing CLAUDE.md's rule, not implementations; diagnose_load_runtime only prints the two integers into a diagnosis context. Method: grep -rnE over platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ excluding _test.go, then reading each hit.

WHY THE HELPER IS NOT THE SHAPE THE SEAT NAMED. The platform ALREADY has the better mechanism: aiservice.TruncatedError + IsTruncated(err), built for bugs_open/019, which uses the provider's own stop signal (stop_reason=max_tokens / done_reason=length) rather than arithmetic. GenerateText returns it as an error, so every ordinary caller doing `if err != nil` is already protected and needs no numeric check at all. A numeric helper introduced without saying that would invite callers to reimplement a worse detector. So the addition is explicitly documented as a BACKSTOP for the only two cases where the structural signal is unavailable: (1) a provider returning a cut answer as a 200 with no error — the reason round 2's llm_reliability HIGH made me keep an arm at all; (2) reading llm_call_log after the fact, where there is no error object, only two integers (cmd/reasoningset's case).

THE DEFECT THE THREE-STATE EXISTS TO PREVENT. Written as a bare boolean, `outTok >= maxTok` is FALSE when usage is unreported (outTok defaults to 0), so 'we could not tell' silently returns as 'the answer was complete'. Those are different claims and must not share a return value. The design decision that carries this is that TruncationUnknown is the ZERO VALUE: a caller who forgets a case, or reads a zeroed struct, lands on the state that forces a decision rather than the one that says fine. Truncated() and Complete() are deliberately NOT complements — exactly one state returns false from both — so `if !state.Truncated() { splice() }` is visibly the mistake, and a test pins that property.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow. This ADDS to platform/aiservice and adopts the helper at ONE call site (my own), with no behaviour change anywhere: ClassifyTruncation(outTok, sentMax) reproduces the previous condition exactly, including the pre-existing `sent > 0` guard, which is now the `maxTokens <= 0 -> Unknown` arm. I did NOT edit cmd/reasoningset: it belongs to another lane, carries its own untouched-twin protection, and changing how it treats UNKNOWN would silently change which rows enter an eval corpus. That finding is reported to them instead, and named here as the one thing this change does not do.

plan.summary: The bugs_open/305 approved round left one reuse advisory: the truncation three-state is inline in rewrite_negations_action.go and should be shared, with the other call sites audited rather than one moved. The audit found the platform already detects truncation STRUCTURALLY (aiservice.TruncatedError/IsTruncated, from the provider's own stop signal), so the numeric rule is only a backstop for two cases: a provider returning a cut answer as a 200 with no error, and post-hoc llm_call_log analysis where no error object exists. This adds aiservice.ClassifyTruncation as an explicitly-documented backstop with three states — the point being that UNKNOWN (usage unreported) must never return as 'complete', which a bare `outTok >= maxTok` boolean does silently. Unknown is the ZERO VALUE, and Truncated()/Complete() are non-complementary. Adopted at one call site with no behaviour change; cmd/reasoningset's two sites are reported to their lane, not edited.

edits.rationale: Add the three-state classifier beside the structural TruncatedError it backs up, so a reader meets the preferred mechanism first. Unknown is the zero value so a forgotten case cannot read as safe; Truncated()/Complete() are non-complementary so the unsafe idiom is visible at the call site.

Each test asserts the absence of the defect rather than the presence of arithmetic, and all three are mutation-proven (evidence below). The zero-value test exists because a const reorder is a silent, plausible future edit that would make an unchecked state read as safe.

Adopt the helper at the site the advisory named. Behaviour-identical: the old condition was `ok && sent > 0 && usageKnown && outTok >= sent`, and ClassifyTruncation returns AtCeiling on exactly that conjunction. The UNKNOWN branch keeps its existing log line and gains the state name so a log census can separate 'could not tell' from 'below'.

grounded_in: platform/aiservice/truncation.go (pre-existing, bugs_open/019): 'So: carry the partial WITH the error. This is deliberately additive — GenerateText's signature is unchanged and every existing caller does `if err != nil { ... }` and is unaffected.' — this is why the numeric helper is documented as a backstop and not as the way to detect truncation.

rewrite_negations_action.go, council round 2 (llm_reliability, HIGH), verbatim in the code today: 'A provider that returns a cut answer as a 200 may report NO usage at all, and `outTok >= sent` with outTok defaulting to 0 is then FALSE — the arm silently never runs, which is indistinguishable from "the answer was complete".'
CLAUDE.md: 'output_tokens == max_tokens means the completion was CUT, not finished. Any agent that rewrites a whole artifact can persist a fragment and report success.'

AUDIT [MEASURED 2026-08-22]: three non-test numeric call sites — rewrite_negations_action.go:535, cmd/reasoningset/main.go:684, cmd/reasoningset/main.go:706. The other three grep hits are comments; diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:1290 only prints max_tokens/output_tokens into a diagnosis context. Method: grep -rnE 'output_?[Tt]okens\s*(>=|==|>)' over platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ minus _test.go, each hit read.

MUTATION EVIDENCE (each test proven to bite, 2026-08-22): (1) dropping `|| outputTokens <= 0` fails 'usage unreported (0) is NOT below' and 'usage negative is NOT below'; (2) reordering the const block so Below takes iota's zero fails TestZeroValueIsUnknown with 'zero value is below_ceiling'; (3) rewriting Truncated() as `s != TruncationBelow` fails TestTruncatedAndCompleteAreNotComplementary with '0 states report neither cut nor complete, want exactly 1'. An earlier attempt at (2) only broke the BUILD, which proves nothing, so it was redone as a compiling mutation.

NOT DONE, deliberately: cmd/reasoningset/main.go:684 and :706 nil-check and skip when usage is unreported, so a success=true row with unreported usage that was actually cut enters the corpus unflagged. That is the same UNKNOWN hole, but changing it changes which rows reach an eval set and belongs to that lane; reported to them rather than edited here.
plan.risks: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: none intended. ClassifyTruncation reproduces the previous conjunction exactly (`ok && sent > 0 && usageKnown && outTok >= sent`), with the old `sent > 0` guard becoming the `maxTokens <= 0 -> Unknown` arm; a reviewer should check that equivalence line by line, since it is the only claim the tests do not prove (they test the helper, not the substitution). SECOND: `options["max_tokens"]` is read with `, _` rather than the previous `, ok` — if the key is absent sentMax is 0, which classifies as Unknown, i.e. the same not-truncated outcome the old `ok` guard produced; confirm that is still true if anyone later makes 0 meaningful. THIRD, the reuse question a reviewer should press on: is adding a numeric classifier at all a risk of callers preferring it to IsTruncated? That is why the doc block leads with 'Prefer it' and names the only two cases; if the seat thinks a comment is not enough on a shared seam, the alternative is to keep the logic inline and close the advisory as WONTFIX with this audit as the reason. FOURTH: nothing in the fleet calls ClassifyTruncation except the one adopted site, so this ships inert beyond it — the accumulated-surface question (RFC_022's optional-key budget) does not apply, as this adds no config key and no action input.
